payload.title: select_candidates cuts the ranked list at --limit (default 20) before mint_candidates drops drifts that are already recorded, so recorded drifts of earlier classes consume the limit and the last-ranked class (graphql_operation_drift) mints nothing.
evidence: tools/aria-poc/seed_drift_findings.py:308-320 (already-recorded subjects are dropped inside the mint loop, after the cut)
tools/aria-poc/seed_drift_findings.py:407-409 (the judge selects with an unlimited list, so closure is unaffected and the starvation stays invisible)
payload.rule_violated: A detector must not silently drop a true finding: the limit is meant to bound new mints, but it also bounds the look at the pool.
payload.notes: With 20 enum or UI drifts already recorded, the seeder slices to exactly those 20, prints '20 already recorded' and never reaches the graphql drifts; the same cut hides drift 21 onward of any class. Not reachable today: the package reviewers report a clean pool of zero drifts, so this is a latent miss. Close condition: Filter recorded subjects first and apply --limit to the new mints, or give each class its own quota. Proven by a seeder test with 20 recorded enum drifts plus one graphql drift that mints the graphql finding. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 5). Verified at origin/main d716541239.
